declared_target.full_name: protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase

short: This is an antibody to PERK (EIF2AK3), the endoplasmic reticulum kinase that coordinates the unfolded protein response. It is not an antibody to phosphorylated ERK1/2, the growth-signalling kinases written p-ERK or pERK. The two are unrelated proteins whose abbreviations differ by a hyphen, and they run at different sizes: PERK at about 125 kDa, ERK1/2 as the familiar double band near 42 and 44 kDa.
explanation: PERK is an abbreviation for protein kinase R-like endoplasmic reticulum kinase, also called EIF2AK3 — a membrane-bound kinase in the endoplasmic reticulum that helps coordinate the unfolded protein response. ERK is an abbreviation for extracellular signal-regulated kinase, a pair of unrelated cytoplasmic kinases (ERK1/MAPK3 and ERK2/MAPK1) in growth, division and survival signalling; phosphorylated ERK is conventionally written p-ERK or pERK. So PERK and p-ERK name two entirely different proteins and differ in print by one hyphen. An antibody to one is not expected to detect the other, and a molecular weight is often the only thing in a published figure that betrays which was used: PERK runs near 125 kDa where ERK1/2 gives a double band near 42 and 44 kDa.
papers_source: The list was compiled by searching indexed full texts for each product code; the published spreadsheet is linked from the article. Only the DOI, the product code and the reviewer's verdict are carried here. Four of the papers the review names carry a PubMed id and no DOI — they are e-Century titles (Am J Transl Res, Am J Cancer Res), which register no DOI with Crossref at all — so they are keyed on the PubMed id instead. That reaches them on PubMed, PMC and Europe PMC; a title and year would also reach them on the publisher's own page, and the review's listing gives no full title to key on.

source.title: PERK vs p-ERK: Another Antibody Confusion!
